title: Impulsivity Testing Protocol
author: Ray Norbury
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.uayesfw

steps.title: Obtain consent and answer questions
steps.instruction: Invite the participant to complete the consent form and be ready to respond to any questions.

steps.title: Assign unique participant identifier
steps.instruction: Add a unique identifier (e.g., RN001 – your initials then the participant number). Each participant should have a different identifier (RN001, RN002 …).

steps.title: Log into testing computer
steps.instruction: Log into the testing computer and navigate to the experimental files on the N‑drive.

steps.title: Locate and prepare experiment folders
steps.instruction: Find the Impulsivity folder on the N‑drive and within it the first task folder (e.g., 1_DD). Ensure file names are correct; if you think you may be at risk of overwriting a file, STOP and CHECK before proceeding.

steps.title: Run experiments in counterbalanced order
steps.instruction: For each experiment (DD, JCT, SST) in a counterbalanced order, launch the task without closing E‑Prime between tasks. When prompted, enter the subject number (1, 2, 3, or 4) and set the session number to 1. After each task, open the next experiment folder, re‑enter the participant details as above, and continue.

substeps.instruction: DD (Delay Discounting): Read the following script to the participant – “We are now going to show you two amounts of money on the screen and we would like you to choose either to take the lesser amount now or the larger amount later. For example, would you rather have £50 now or £100 in ten years? If you would like to take the money now press the ‘z’ key, if you would rather wait press the ‘m’ key. As you make your choices the money available may change. In each case simply continue with your choices as I described. You will not be given the money presented – the amounts are purely hypothetical – but you should respond as if you were getting the money. We will start with a few examples so you can get the hang of it. If you have any questions at the end of the practice block please let me know.”

JCT (Jar Choice Task): Read the following script – “We are going to show you 2 jars, A and B. In jar A the ratio of blue to red discs is 85:15, in Jar B the ratio is reversed, i.e. there are 15 blue discs and 85 red discs. Next we will ask you a question about the proportions. Specifically we will ask you to estimate the probability of drawing a blue disc from jar A? We will then proceed to the main part of the task. For each trial you will be shown a disc (either red or blue) and you will be offered the choice to see another disc or guess which jar the disc is drawn from. If you want to see another disc press the key ‘d’; the disc will be replaced in the jar and a second disc drawn at random. If you are pretty certain you know which jar the bead came from then you should select the jar (the letter ‘j’). You will then be asked to indicate which jar you think the disc came from and how positive (as a percentage) you are about your choice. There are 5 sets of trials; in each set draws will be taken from the same jar and the disc is replaced after each draw.”

SST (Stop‑Signal Task): Read the following script – “For this task please place the first and index fingers of your dominant hand on the ‘ ’ symbols on the keyboard. I will then start the task. You will watch the screen carefully and respond as quickly as possible to the arrow symbol by pressing the corresponding key, so if the ‘ ’ symbol appears press the ‘>’ key as quickly as possible. Occasionally the ‘<>’ symbol will turn red; if it does you should inhibit your response (i.e., try not to press the key). The game starts with a few practice trials to get you going. Remember you should always try to respond as quickly as possible.”

steps.title: Confirm data files generated
steps.instruction: When you have finished the experiments, verify that each experimental folder contains the important output files ending with .edat2 (e.g., 1_DD-1-1.edat2) and .txt (e.g., 1_DD-1-1.txt).

steps.title: Debrief participant and collect forms
steps.instruction: Thank the participant and give them a copy of the debrief form, making sure the participant identifier is included on the form.

steps.title: Email data files to supervisor
steps.instruction: Email all *.edat2 and *.txt files from the session to the supervisor.

steps.title: Leave data files unchanged
steps.instruction: Do not rename any files, move any files into different folders, or run any macros on the data.

steps.title: Seek assistance if unsure
steps.instruction: If you have any doubt about these instructions, speak to the supervisor to avoid losing data.
